category_title: Student with language impairment who shouts out and disrupts others to avoid difficult tasks
student_description: James is a 9-year-old with a language impairment who frequently exhibits off-task and disruptive behavior (shouting, refusing work) to escape challenging tasks due to a history of repeated academic failure. He uniquely requires high rates of specific teacher attention during difficult work and carefully calibrated independent tasks to maintain appropriate behavior and build a sense of success.

criteria.rationale: James has a history of repeated failure; providing independent tasks he can complete with high accuracy prevents task-avoidance behaviors.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes a strategy to ensure independent assignments are calibrated to an easy level (e.g., 80%+ accuracy) for James to complete without assistance.

criteria.rationale: Completely avoiding hard tasks creates dependency, so James needs a structured way to approach difficult work without being left alone to fail.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes a method for supporting James through challenging tasks (e.g., pairing hard tasks with high teacher attention) rather than simply removing difficult work from his curriculum.
